SELECTED_INDEX: 9
CONFIDENCE: 0.31
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows all of the key signatures of an aromatic nitro-amide containing an aliphatic side chain:  
• Very strong νs(NO₂) near 1395 cm⁻¹ and medium νas(NO₂) around 1563 cm⁻¹ confirm a nitro group.  
• A carbonyl band at 1677 cm⁻¹ matches an amide/ester C=O rather than an aldehyde or ketone.  
• Weak N–H stretches appear at 3124–3187 cm⁻¹, consistent with the secondary amide NH present in candidate 9.  
• Strong aliphatic C–H stretch at 2896 cm⁻¹ requires at least one sp³ C–H; candidate 9 has a vinyl-methyl group, whereas most other nitro-aromatic candidates lack sp³ C–H.  
• Aromatic C–H stretches at 3056 cm⁻¹, ring C=C at 1605 cm⁻¹ and out-of-plane NO₂ wags at 683/611 cm⁻¹ are all compatible with the substituted benzene ring of candidate 9.  
Taken together, C/C=C/NC(=O)Oc1cccc([N+](=O)[O-])c1 (candidate 9) best accounts for the observed nitro, amide C=O, NH, aliphatic CH, and aromatic features, making it the most consistent choice among the provided structures.
